transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-17 | Start: 15:30 UTC | Duration: ~54m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Luca Patel (Redwood SE), Ravi Singh (Redwood CSM) - Jordan Reyes (CTO), Priya Natarajan (DevOps), Elena Morales (Compliance) - Blue Lantern Health

Summary (auto): Kickoff orientation for implementation, clarify access and network, review security/compliance asks (SOC2/KMS/SAML), confirm staging access and pilot scope for Dedicated deployment.

00:00 Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time, I think we have about 50 minutes, uh two parts — orientation then access/network stuff, feel free to jump in.
00:22 Jordan (CTO): Yeah thanks, Maya. We're excited, want to make sure this goes smooth; main ask is predictable latency for triage workflows and strict PHI controls.
00:38 Luca (Redwood SE): Great, quick intro from our side — I'm Luca, I'll own the pilot benchmarks and runtime config. We'll propose a Dedicated pool for predictable throughput but can discuss hosted fallbacks.
00:52 Priya (DevOps): Quick note — our security team wants VPC-based connectivity, KMS integration, and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. Elena is on for compliance questions.
01:07 Elena (Compliance): Hi — SOC2 is required, also an attestation for data residency and retention. Do you keep verbatim logs?
01:18 Maya: Short answer: by default logs are retained per plan, and we have enterprise retention controls. We'll send SOC2 and retention matrix after this call.
01:31 Jordan: Sounds good. On the latency side, our SLO is 150ms p95 for 512-token inference for our triage path; cost target is also important.
01:42 Luca: Ok 150ms p95 is tight — depends on sequence length, batching, and whether KV cache can be warmed. For Dedicated we can tune kernels and batch size to hit that — but if you need cryptographic isolation we recommend private deployment.
02:05 Priya: When you say private deployment, is that on our VPC or an on-prem box?
02:12 Luca: We have two variants: Redwood Private in your VPC (customer-managed network, our control plane optional), or on-prem package for air-gapped setups. Both integrate with KMS/HSM for keywrap.
02:30 Elena: For compliance we'll need KMS with key rotation logs and HSM mention — do you support external HSMs?
02:38 Maya: Yes, we support customer-managed KMS including HSM-backed keys; will include integration notes.
02:44 Jordan: Can you summarize the difference between Dedicated and Hosted again — in plain language?
02:51 Maya: Hosted is fastest to start, usage-based, but less isolation. Dedicated is reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput and isolation, monthly commit. Private adds VPC/on-prem and extra controls for compliance.
03:12 Priya: Ok. For our pilot we'd prefer Dedicated in our cloud region with VPC peering; hostnames and egress rules we can provide.
03:22 Luca: That works — we'll need a staging VPC CIDR and a few egress IPs to allow. Also we'll ask for a small firewall rule for health checks.
03:35 Priya: Noted. Who's setting up the peering? (laugh)
03:38 Jordan: We'll have DevOps own it but Redwood to provide the network steps.
03:45 Maya: We'll send a network checklist and an example terraform snippet.
03:52 Ravi (CSM): We typically run a 2-week pilot: week 1 smoke + connectivity, week 2 load/p95 tuning. Does that align?
04:02 Jordan: Yes, two weeks is fine. We want to run our eval prompts and a small load test to confirm latency and cost per token.
04:14 Luca: For the load test we'll use a synthetic traffic profile that matches your 75th/95th percentile sequence lengths. Also we'll exercise KV cache for conversation flows to emulate production.
04:30 Priya: A couple of practical questions — who will get console access in staging and how is RBAC handled?
04:38 Maya: RBAC is via SSO/SAML and we can map roles to your IdP groups. We'll request a list of admin users for initial access.
04:50 Elena: Do you produce detailed audit logs with token-level metadata for compliance? We can't have raw PHI stored in logs.
04:58 Luca: We support token-level cost/latency breakdowns, but for PHI-sensitive workloads we recommend redaction and prefix-only logging. We can enable redaction pipelines and route logs to your SIEM instead of persisting full payloads.
05:18 Elena: Good. Please include the redaction options in the security pack.
05:24 Maya: Will do.
05:26 Jordan: On model governance — can we pin model versions and have rollbacks?
05:33 Luca: Yes, model pinning and rollouts (canary/A-B) are supported. We also have automatic fallback policies if capacity is constrained — useful for high-availability.
05:46 Jordan: Any notes about quantized model artifacts? We might want to use int8 to save cost.
05:52 Luca: We recommend model and quantization suggestions per workload — Redwood Optimize can surface recommendations, and in Dedicated we'll test int8 to ensure quality parity before rolling out.
06:08 Priya: Network: do you need a VPN or just VPC peering?
06:12 Maya: Peering is sufficient for Dedicated in your cloud region; for on-prem we use a VPN or private link. We'll include both options in the network checklist.
06:23 Jordan: Can we do a short demo of the staging console access? Maybe later this week?
06:28 Maya: Yes — we'll include a live demo as part of the connectivity window once peering is in place.
06:35 Priya: Regarding secrets: where do prompts and API keys live? We prefer keys rotated via KMS.
06:42 Luca: API credentials can be stored in your KMS and we support managed key wrapping. We'll provide examples for key rotation and limited-scope tokens.
06:52 Elena: A compliance thing — retention and deletion guarantees. If a user data subject requests deletion, how quickly can you purge?
06:59 Maya: We have APIs for data deletion; SLA for purge is configurable in enterprise plans, typical target 24–72 hours depending on retention tier. We'll include the deletion API docs.
07:16 Jordan: Great. Any vendor lock-in concerns? We do not want a heavy migration cost.
07:22 Luca: You can export model artifacts and we support standard model formats; inference runtime configs are documented for portability. We'll highlight migration steps in the playbook.
07:36 Priya: Ok on I/O. For the pilot, what's the minimal telemetry we need to provide for the load tests?
07:43 Luca: Just a sample of request patterns: average tokens, 95th tokens, concurrency target. We'll also need sample prompt set for quality checks.
07:52 Jordan: We'll send that by Friday.
07:55 Maya: Perfect.
08:00 Ravi: Quick note on billing — pilot costs are usually covered on usage with a capped estimate; we'll follow up with a forecast.
08:08 Jordan: Good. Please ensure we have a clear number for projected monthly cost at target throughput.
08:14 Maya: We'll include a cost estimate in the follow-up.
08:17 Priya: Any dependencies on cloud provider-specific features? We run primarily on GCP but with us-east and europe-west regions.
08:25 Luca: We support multiple regions. Some kernel optimizations differ by GPU type, we'll surface recommended instance types for your region.
08:36 Elena: About data residency — if we keep logs in eu-west, can the control plane be in a separate region?
08:43 Maya: The control plane can be in our central region while data plane stays in your region for Private deployments; we'll document the architecture choices.
08:55 Jordan: Ok. Let's talk timeline — when can we start the peering and pilot?
09:01 Priya: We can start networking next week if we get the checklist.
09:06 Maya: We'll send the checklist and SOC2 today; target peering by 2026-09-22, pilot start 2026-09-27 pending access.
09:17 Jordan: Works for us.
09:20 Luca: Technical deep dive — do you want a separate SE session on kernel tuning and batch configuration?
09:26 Priya: Yes please, especially around KV cache and sequence length impact. We want to avoid surprises later.
09:33 Luca: We'll schedule a 60-minute SE deep dive ASAP — propose 2026-09-24.
09:39 Maya: Noted.
09:42 Elena: One more compliance Q — can we get a sample of your audit log schema?
09:48 Maya: Included in the security pack.
09:50 Jordan: Ok let's recap next steps.
09:54 Maya: Recap — Maya will send SOC2, security pack, network checklist + terraform snippet by EOD; Priya to share CIDR and peering contacts by 2026-09-22; Luca to prepare pilot test plan and SE deep dive on 2026-09-24; schedule pilot week of 2026-09-27.
10:20 Jordan: Thanks all. Any blockers from our side?
10:25 Priya: Nothing else, we'll assemble contact list.
10:30 Maya: Great. We'll also attach an example runbook and the console access guide.
10:40 Ravi: I'll follow up in CRM with the kickoff ticket and next meeting invite.
10:45 Jordan: Perfect. Thanks everyone, talk soon.
